author: StefaniaHergane
title: Debian Packages job fails - apt-get cannot resolve archive.ubuntu.com mirrors (DNS resolution failure)
signature: temporary failure resolving ubuntu archive mirror hosts during apt get update package has no installation candidate|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get update/install fails because archive.ubuntu.com, azure.archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com could not be DNS-resolved inside the container.

key_errors:
Err:1 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy InRelease
  Temporary failure resolving 'archive.ubuntu.com'
W: Failed to fetch http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/dists/jammy/InRelease  Temporary failure resolving 'archive.ubuntu.com'
W: Some index files failed to download. They have been ignored, or old ones used instead.

E: Package 'gnupg' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package wget
E: Package 'ca-certificates' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package lsb-release
##[error]Process completed with exit code 100.
root_cause: The 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step runs apt-get update/install inside a container, and DNS resolution for archive.ubuntu.com, azure.archive.ubuntu.com, and security.ubuntu.com intermittently failed ('Temporary failure resolving'), causing apt to fall back to stale/empty package indexes. As a result several base packages (gnupg, wget, ca-certificates, lsb-release) had no installation candidate and the step exited with code 100. This is a transient runner/container DNS or network outage, not caused by the PR under test (PR #39532 only touches NPU compiler-adapter C++ source and a unit test, unrelated to debian packaging).
reproduction_steps: N/A - transient DNS resolution failure on GitHub-hosted runner's container network; not reliably reproducible locally. Re-running the failed job is the standard mitigation.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job (DNS outage is expected to clear on retry).
Consider adding a DNS retry/backoff wrapper or an explicit resolver (e.g. retry apt-get update with exponential backoff) around the apt-get step in job_debian_packages.yml to reduce flakiness.
Monitor recurrence: this exact signature has now been seen 4+ times within 12 hours; if it continues, escalate to infra/runner team to check the self-hosted/azure mirror DNS path.
prevention_strategies: Add retry logic (e.g. `apt-get update` with a small retry loop) around network-dependent steps in job_debian_packages.yml, and/or pre-pull dependencies into a cached base image so flaky upstream Ubuntu mirror DNS does not block the merge queue.
historical_context: Same signature (hash d734e6d0da3ffc69) has been recorded 4 times between 2026-11-11T14:34:10Z and 2026-11-11T16:19:57Z, affecting PRs #39262 and #39693 — this run is the 5th occurrence in the same window, confirming an active, ongoing DNS/network issue on the merge-queue runners rather than an isolated incident. A related but distinct signature (different wording, 'Could not connect'/'Unable to connect' to azure.archive.ubuntu.com) was seen repeatedly around 2026-08-18/19.
